title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: Student (EE1) is exposed to the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login and submission process. The student's identity is transmitted to the external system, which may be used to identify the student for grading purposes.
assumptions: The student's identity is not encrypted or obfuscated during transmission.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the portal explicitly stores or uses the student's identity for grading.

title: Data Access by External Entity
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) is accessed by an external entity (EE1). The process of logging in and submitting an assignment exposes sensitive student data (student id, course, work file) to the external system.
assumptions: The portal does not implement secure authentication or data masking.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the portal uses secure authentication mechanisms.

title: Identifier Exposure
description: The data flow transmits student identifiers (student id, course, file reference) from the Portal Web App (P1) to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) as the data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject.

title: Identifier Exposure
description: The data flow transmits student identifiers (student id, course, file reference) from the Assignment & Grading Service (P2) back to the Portal Web App (P1). This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) as the data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject.

title: Assignment File Disclosure
description: The assignment file containing student personal data (student id, course, submission time) is transferred from the Assignment & Grading Service (Process P2) to the Assignment Store (DataStore DS1). This constitutes a Data Disclosure (D) threat as it represents the transfer of personal data across a boundary.

title: Assignment File Disclosure
description: The assignment file containing student personal data is transferred from the Assignment Store (DataStore DS1) to the Assignment & Grading Service (Process P2). This constitutes a Data Disclosure (D) threat as it represents the transfer of personal data across a boundary.

title: Teacher's Data Access
description: Teacher (EE3) requests and processes the queue of submissions to review for their courses, which may contain personally identifiable information (PII) or sensitive data.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the queue of submissions and the system processes this data for review purposes.

title: System Data Processing
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes the queue of submissions, which may include sensitive data accessed by the teacher.
assumptions: The system processes the queue of submissions for review.

title: Data Leakage
description: Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) may inadvertently expose student names, work content, and submission times to the external Teacher entity (EE3) without proper access controls or encryption.
assumptions: The portal is accessible to the teacher, and the teacher has the necessary permissions to view this data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the teacher has explicit permission to view this specific data set. Assuming access is granted for the purpose of this analysis.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: External Entity EE3 (Teacher) may access or exfiltrate student data (names, work content, submission times) from the portal without authorization.
assumptions: Teacher has access to the portal interface.
uncertainty_note: Assuming teacher has access to the portal interface for the purpose of this analysis.

title: Teacher records grade
description: Teacher (EE3) records a grade for a student, which may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., student ID, grade value) that is not encrypted or protected during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App (P1).
assumptions: The teacher has access to the student's personal data and the system allows direct data transfer.

title: Teacher records feedback
description: Teacher (EE3) records written feedback for a student, which may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., student ID, feedback text) that is not encrypted or protected during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App (P1).
assumptions: The teacher has access to the student's personal data and the system allows direct data transfer.

title: Grades Portal Web App receives grade
description: Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives a grade from the Teacher (EE3), which may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., student ID, grade value) that is not encrypted or protected during transmission from the Teacher.
assumptions: The Grades Portal Web App has access to the teacher's input and the system allows direct data transfer.

title: Grades Portal Web App receives feedback
description: Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives written feedback from the Teacher (EE3), which may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., student ID, feedback text) that is not encrypted or protected during transmission from the Teacher.
assumptions: The Grades Portal Web App has access to the teacher's input and the system allows direct data transfer.

title: Grade Record Exposure
description: The assignment service (P2) writes grade records (student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, timestamp) to the Grade Records Database (DS2). If the database is not properly secured or if the write operation is not restricted to authorized users, sensitive student and course information could be exposed.
assumptions: Assumes the database is not already fully secured.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the database is fully secured; this is a general risk.

title: Data Store Exposure
description: The Grade Records Database (DS2) is a data store. If the database is not properly secured or if the write operation is not restricted to authorized users, sensitive student and course information could be exposed.
assumptions: Assumes the database is not already fully secured.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the database is fully secured; this is a general risk.

title: Unauthorized Access to Personal Data
description: External entity (Student) requests and receives personally identifiable information (PII) from the system without explicit consent or a valid data flow model.
assumptions: The student has not explicitly authorized the system to access their personal grades and feedback.

title: Data Processing of Personal Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes personally identifiable information (PII) from the student without a valid data flow model or explicit consent.
assumptions: The system processes student grades and feedback without a documented data flow model.

title: Grade Display to Student
description: Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) displays student grades to ExternalEntity EE1 (Student). This interaction is valid (Process->ExternalEntity) and exposes sensitive personal data (grades) to an external entity without appropriate access controls or encryption.

title: Student Access to Grades
description: ExternalEntity EE1 (Student) accesses and views their own grades. This is a valid interaction (ExternalEntity->Process) but the student entity itself is an external entity, and the threat analysis here focuses on the flow from the portal to the student. However, the primary threat is the data exposure from P1 to EE1.

title: Unauthorized Grade Access
description: Parent (EE2) logs in and requests their child's grades. If the parent account is not properly linked to the child account, or if the system does not enforce access control based on the parent-child relationship, an unauthorized individual could access the child's grades.
assumptions: The parent account is linked to the child account.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the system enforces access control based on the parent-child relationship.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) processes data from Parent (EE2). If the system does not validate the parent-child relationship before processing the request, the parent's account could be used to access the child's grades.
assumptions: The system does not validate the parent-child relationship before processing the request.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the system validates the parent-child relationship.

title: Grade Display to Parent
description: Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) displays child's grades, feedback, and submission history to ExternalEntity EE2 (Parent). This interaction is valid under the Process->ExternalEntity mapping table, but the display of sensitive personal data (grades, feedback, history) to an external entity without explicit consent or a data processing agreement constitutes a privacy risk.
assumptions: The parent entity has no contractual or legal obligation to receive this specific data set.

title: Parent Access to Child's Data
description: ExternalEntity EE2 (Parent) is receiving data from Process P1. The mapping table indicates this is a valid interaction (ExternalEntity->Process). However, the parent entity is accessing sensitive personal data (grades, feedback, history) without a clear data processing agreement or explicit consent mechanism, which is a privacy risk.
assumptions: The parent entity has no contractual or legal obligation to receive this specific data set.

title: Unauthorized Account Creation
description: ExternalEntity (EE4) creates accounts without proper authorization or verification.

title: Unauthorized Account Modification
description: ExternalEntity (EE4) modifies account details (names, emails, roles) without authorization.

title: Unauthorized Account Disabling
description: ExternalEntity (EE4) disables accounts without authorization.

title: Unauthorized Account Creation
description: Process (P1) creates accounts without proper authorization or verification.

title: Unauthorized Account Modification
description: Process (P1) modifies account details (names, emails, roles) without authorization.

title: Unauthorized Account Disabling
description: Process (P1) disables accounts without authorization.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grading Service
description: An unauthorized user or process may access the grading service (P2) to view or modify account records or parent-child relationship links before they are written to the account directory (DS3).

title: Data Modification by Unauthorized Actor
description: An unauthorized actor may modify the account records or parent-child relationship links stored in the grading service (P2) without proper authorization, potentially introducing errors or security vulnerabilities.

title: Unauthorized Access to Account Directory
description: An unauthorized user or process may access the account directory (DS3) to view or modify account records or parent-child relationship links, bypassing the grading service's controls.

title: Data Modification by Unauthorized Actor
description: An unauthorized actor may modify the account records or parent-child relationship links stored in the account directory (DS3) without proper authorization, potentially introducing errors or security vulnerabilities.

title: Data Disclosure to External Entity
description: The process P2 (Assignment & Grading Service) transfers full grade records, assignments, and account directory to the external entity EE5 (Cloud Hosting Provider). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system is transferring personal data to a third party without a direct data store intermediate step, violating the minimality principle.

title: Data Disclosure from External Entity
description: The external entity EE5 (Cloud Hosting Provider) is receiving data from the process P2. While the mapping table excludes ExternalEntity->ExternalEntity flows, the context implies EE5 may be acting as a data store or intermediary. If EE5 is acting as a data store, it would be transferring data to another external entity, which is an invalid interaction. If EE5 is acting as a process, it is receiving data from P2, which is a valid Process->ExternalEntity interaction. However, given the context of 'hosting replication' and 'third-party cloud hosting provider', EE5 is likely acting as a data store or a process acting as a data store. If it acts as a data store, it is transferring data to another external entity, which is invalid. If it acts as a process, it is receiving data from P2, which is valid. However, the threat type D at EE5 implies EE5 is the originator of a data disclosure, which would mean EE5 is transferring data to another external entity, which is invalid. Therefore, the threat at EE5 is invalid.
uncertainty_note: The threat at EE5 is invalid because the mapping table explicitly excludes ExternalEntity->ExternalEntity interactions. EE5 is acting as a data store or a process acting as a data store, but it is not transferring data to another external entity.

title: Grade Records Access
description: DataStore DS2 (Grade Records Database) is accessed by Process P2 (Assignment & Grading Service) to build views for students, parents, and teachers. This interaction is valid under the mapping table (DataStore->Process).
assumptions: The data flow is legitimate and authorized.

title: Grade Records Access
description: Process P2 (Assignment & Grading Service) accesses DataStore DS2 (Grade Records Database) to retrieve grade records for building views.
assumptions: The data flow is legitimate and authorized.
